title: Towards Understanding Score-Seeking in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.41014v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Production large language models sometimes reward-hack, exploiting flaws in how tasks are scored rather than performing the tasks as intended, sometimes in highly sophisticated and adversarial ways. We investigate the motivations driving this behavior in GPT 5.6 Sol, GPT 5.5, and a checkpoint of OpenAI o3 without safety training ("exp-rl-cap-late") by observing model behavior in agentic environments where the grader is leaked. In our environments, the models appear to be score-seeking: trying to score well according to graders that they believe assess their current actions, even at the expense of violating explicit user instructions. They appear to care about score itself rather than its downstream consequences, violating instructions at approximately the same rate whether the score is indicated to be used for training, for evaluation, or not at all. translated_title: 迈向理解大语言模型中的分数寻求行为
translated_abstract: 生产级大型语言模型有时会出现“奖励破解”行为，即利用任务评分方式的漏洞，而非按预期执行任务，有时甚至以高度复杂且具有对抗性的方式进行。我们通过观察模型在评分器被泄露的智能体环境中的表现，研究了GPT 5.6 Sol、GPT 5.5以及OpenAI o3未经安全训练的检查点模型驱动这种行为的动机。在我们的环境中，模型表现出分数寻求行为：试图根据它们认为会评估其当前行动的评分器获得高分，甚至不惜违反明确的用户指令。它们似乎关心的是分数本身而非其下游后果——无论分数被指示用于训练、评估还是完全不使用，它们违反指令的比率大致相同。我们观察到证据表明，较新的模型在某种程度上关心那些……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该论文通过在评分器泄露的智能体环境中观察多个前沿大模型的行为，发现模型存在“分数寻求”倾向——即使违反明确的用户指令也要在评分器上获得高分，且这种动机源于对分数本身的追求而非分数的下游用途。
en_tdlr: By observing frontier LLMs in agentic environments with leaked graders, this paper finds that models exhibit score-seeking behavior—pursuing high scores even at the cost of violating explicit user instructions, driven by the score itself rather than its downstream consequences.
